title: CLO Tips Workshop - Strap Lacing
description: CLO technical expert teaches you how to add strap designs to your 3D corset within ten minutes!
transcript:
How to Tie a String to a Model  
Today's small tip is about tying a string to a model.  
Now you can see that the 3D window displays a breastplate.  
Other panels have been simulated on the model.  
The area behind this pin is fixed with a transparent panel.  
Then change the transparency of this panel’s fabric to 0.  
The panel can be hidden in the 3D window.  
Start creating the string effect below.  
These panels can be selected before creation.  
This string panel does not need to be selected.  
Wait a moment for the simulation.  
Right-click on the selected panel.  
After freezing,  
you will see that this panel is transparent,  
but it still exists.  
To simulate it without conflict,  
you can right-click to reactivate it,  
so this panel does not participate in the simulation.  
Switch to the 2D window.  
Look at the basic lines on this panel.  
First, use the hook outline tool  
to frame these circles.  
After framing the selection,  
right-click on the selected line,  
cut it, and sew it.  
Because this circle needs to wait,  
it is cut and sewn.  
After cutting, use the adjustment panel tool,  
select these panels,  
and move these small panels outward  
for easier operation at the back.  
This side is also moved out slightly.  
Now move this panel down first.  
Next, create the string effect.  
For the string,  
first move this panel inward  
to create the effect from the inside.  
Before creating,  
you can add an inner line on this panel  
because it needs to be sewn with tape.  
Use the edit panel tool  
to measure its length—about 5 mm.  
Use the inner multidirectional tool  
to create a 5 mm line,  
slightly oblique,  
about 5 mm.  
Double-click to finish.  
After adjusting the number, you can slightly fine-tune it,  
a little downward,  
because shortly you will sew the tape.  
Now after drawing the line,  
you can see only one.  
For other panels, you can select the inner line,  
then copy it.  
For the next one,  
you can't just copy all at once and paste it,  
because some panels differ,  
and placing them all at once causes deviations.  
So you need to copy them one by one.  
After doing this,  
you can sew the panel below.  
Use the sewing tool  
to sew it.  
Show the panel,  
switch to texture surface view.  
You will see the panel is facing the opposite direction.  
You can select it,  
rotate it,  
push it inward,  
then simulate.  
Now one is done.  
After finishing,  
select this panel,  
reduce its particle diameter,  
adjust it to 5,  
set collision to 1,  
remonitor,  
and click the control button to simulate.  
Pause the simulation.  
One is done.  
Next is the effect of binding the tape.  
You can copy it.  
Select the panel,  
press Ctrl C and Ctrl V to copy and paste,  
place it below,  
then adjust it.  
After that, sew it.  
Open the panel to show the inner line,  
use the sewing tool,  
and sew in the 3D window.  
Click the two lines to sew.  
Good simulation.  
Pause the simulation.  
Use the adjustment panel tool,  
select the panel,  
then copy one,  
rotate it,  
use the sewing tool,  
sew in the 3D window.  
Good simulation.  
Now one is done.  
After finishing,  
you can see  
it comes out from the top,  
but it should be at the bottom.  
So we use the sewing tool.  
Select the sewing tool,  
go straight to frame selection.  
Because the bottom panel is frozen,  
you can't select it.  
After frame selection,  
click sewing selection,  
use the positioning ball to move inward.  
Move the other side inward as well,  
then simulate.  
Pause the simulation.  
The side effect is good.  
Click the adjustment panel.  
Continue using the same method below  
to make the second one.  
Use the adjustment panel tool,  
select the panel,  
after frame selection,  
copy (Ctrl C),  
paste (Ctrl V),  
then place it below.  
After placing it down,  
adjust its position,  
then use the sewing tool,  
sew in the 3D window.  
Good simulation.  
After finishing,  
open the simulation.  
After the simulation,  
use the same grid tool,  
select the grid,  
push it inward,  
push it inward here too.  
Good simulation.  
Using the same method,  
you can continue making it downward.  
But when you do the lower part,  
you will find the top frame is slightly farther,  
and the bottom frame is slightly closer.  
So when you copy the selection,  
after copying,  
double-click to activate the center point,  
then shorten the two panels a bit.  
After adjusting,  
use the sewing tool to sew,  
simulate,  
then use the grid tool,  
push it inward,  
simulate.  
Use the same method for  
these panels below,  
make all the rest.  
Good simulation.  
After a while,  
there is still one left.  
You should copy a board,  
place it down,  
adjust its location,  
rotate it.  
After sewing, the bandage is all made,  
then switch the texture back to thick texture display.  
There should be one at the bottom.  
For the effect of tying the butterfly knot,  
we can prepare the butterfly knot in advance.  
Enlarge it.  
This is the butterfly knot made in advance, place it on.  
After making the butterfly knot, you can check it.  
Adjust its position.  
After that, you can use a sewing thread or sewing tool to fix it together.  
Simulate.  
The butterfly knot is almost done.  
Close the window.  
There needs to be an eyelet in the bandage.  
The eyelet can be created with a button.  
In the 3D window,  
find the button tool.  
Add a button on the board,  
probably in the middle.  
Click to add a button.  
After adding, it defaults to this kind of button.  
In the object window, select it as a button.  
In the attribute editor below, click on shape.  
You can choose a grommet preset,  
for example, the first one.  
The first one will be relatively large.  
You can modify the specifications,  
for example, change it to 11.  
11 is about the same size.  
Now one has been added.  
You can select it.  
Use the move button tool,  
select the button,  
then copy and paste (Ctrl C, Ctrl V) to create a second button.  
Click to add.  
Then copy and paste.  
The following buttons are the same.  
It should be almost done.  
When pasting,  
hold the Shift key.  
The layer lowers.  
At the same time, right-click,  
play the dialogue frame.  
You can add multiple buttons at once.  
Add 7 in total.  
Then click to confirm.  
After confirmation, you will find  
some distance deviations with the back buttons.  
It may be because the positions of these grommets  
and the structure itself differ.  
So adding multiple buttons at once  
causes a slight position bias.  
It doesn’t matter.  
You can select a button to delete.  
Select the button above,  
copy one,  
then click near the button area to add one.  
Now half are added.  
For the other half, select all the buttons,  
on the selected buttons above, right-click.  
Copy to one side.  
Click to copy quickly.  
After copying is complete,  
select these buttons,  
you can turn off collision,  
change the line length to a negative number,  
for example, change it to -2.  
If you change the number of points,  
the button will automatically adjust.  
Set this button to -2.  
It may not be enough,  
you can go a bit further,  
-3,  
-3,  
about 2.5.  
Then select the button,  
change its attribute,  
type to metal effect.  
Select these small 7-hole plates.  
Because now they can be seen in the 3D window,  
you can apply a transparent plate material attribute,  
make it transparent,  
turn off internal line display.  
Now the tape is a bit too thin.  
You can select these tape plates,  
increase their rendering thickness a little,  
for example, adjust to 1.  
The effect of 7-hole threading is done.  
Other plates can be activated.  
The above is the threading effect.  
You can use this method.  
That's all.  
Thanks for watching.  
Please subscribe to my channel,  
and I will see you soon.  
Bye bye.

chunks.title: CLO Tips Workshop - Strap Lacing
chunks.content: ## Overview of Strap Lacing Technique in CLO This section explains how to simulate strap lacing on a 3D garment model using CLO software. Key terms include panels, simulation, sewing tool, adjustment panel tool, string effect, butterfly knot, and eyelets (grommets). The process involves manipulating panels and lines, sewing parts together, and adding details like knots and eyelets for realistic strap lacing effects. --- ## Preparing the Model and Panels for String Effect This section covers setting up the 3D model and panels to create the strap string effect, including visibility adjustments and panel positioning. - In the 3D window, select the breastplate model with simulated panels. - Fix a transparent panel behind the pin area and set its fabric transparency to 0 to hide it without deleting. - Freeze the selected panel via right-click to make it transparent but still present in the simulation. - Reactivate or freeze panels as needed to prevent conflicts during simulation. - Switch to the 2D window and use the hook outline tool to frame circles on the panel. - Cut and sew lines on the panel to prepare for string creation. - Use the adjustment panel tool to move smaller panels outward for easier access, and move the main panel down for better workspace. --- ## Creating and Sewing the String Effect This section details drawing inner lines, copying inner lines across panels, and sewing panels to simulate the strap strings. - Add an inner line about 5 mm long and slightly oblique on the panel using the inner multidirectional tool. - Copy inner lines panel-by-panel rather than all at once to avoid misalignment. - Sew the panels together using the sewing tool. - Rotate panels as necessary to correct orientation, pushing them inward before simulating. - Adjust particle diameter to 5 and set collision to 1 for better simulation accuracy. - Pause simulation to verify progress. - Copy and paste panels to create the effect of binding tape, then sew these new panels. - Use frame selection and positioning tools to align panels correctly, especially when bottom panels are frozen and unselectable. - Continue this process downward, adjusting panel lengths and positions to maintain proportional spacing. - Use the grid tool to push panels inward after sewing for realistic depth in simulation. --- ## Creating the Butterfly Knot Detail This section explains how to add a butterfly knot to the strap lacing for added realism. - Prepare the butterfly knot separately and enlarge it. - Place the butterfly knot on the model in the desired position. - Use the sewing thread or sewing tool to fix the butterfly knot in place. - Simulate to verify proper attachment and appearance. --- ## Adding Eyelets (Grommets) Using the Button Tool This section describes creating eyelets for the strap lacing using the button tool in CLO. - In the 3D window, find and select the button tool. - Add a button (eyelet) on the panel, typically in the middle.
